audit.whatIsWrong: The chart reads Darius / Darius / Skill / Darius / Skill / Darius / Darius, but whys[2] says 'Level 3 E Apprehend lets you pull past his Pillar for a full combo', whys[4] says 'At 6 your R executes him before his sustain and stat-steal can save him', and whys[6] says 'By two-plus items Trundle's ... out-DPS your five stacks in a long duel, taking the lane'. Three cells contradict the sentence printed next to them.
audit.why: The packet chart is Darius / Darius / Darius / Darius / Darius / Darius / Trundle at a 54.45% Darius win rate over 1078 games — identical to what all seven whys already describe. Level 3 is where Apprehend arrives and Trundle has no answer to being dragged off Frozen Domain; level 6 is a true-damage execute against a champion whose only defence is stolen resistances. Two-plus items genuinely goes to Trundle, and the chart is the only place that does not say so.
audit.corrected: win[2] and win[4] to Darius, win[6] to Trundle, in both layers as one group with ratings realigned.
sources: internal contradiction with whys[2], whys[4], whys[6]

audit.whatIsWrong: The Level 6 phase text carries the LaTeX fragment 'R = d + a \times Stacks'. Trundle's spikes are listed as 'Subjugate online, level 6, first item' with no cooldown anywhere.
audit.why: Subjugate is 120/100/80 — the single longest cooldown in the lane and the reason the level 6 and first-item stages differ at all. Frozen Domain is 18s falling to 14s and Pillar of Ice 21s falling to 15s; Chomp is 3.5s, which is why it is not a spike and cannot be waited out.
audit.corrected: Plain-language Level 6 text and the real cooldowns written into the phases, spikes, dos/don'ts and breakdown.cooldowns.

audit.whatIsWrong: The entry says Chomp steals attack speed in four places — spikes[2] 'his Q attack-speed steal', spikes[3] 'Q attack-speed drain', wants.foe[0] 'Drain your attack speed and AD with Q', whys[6] 'attack-speed drain'. It also credits his sustain to 'bite sustain' and never names King's Tribute, and nowhere says what Subjugate does not do.
audit.why: Riot's text for Chomp: 'dealing damage, briefly slowing and sapping some of their Attack Damage' — no attack speed at all. The attack speed comes from Frozen Domain, a separate ability that also grants move speed and increased healing from all sources while he stands on it. His minion sustain is King's Tribute, which heals him a percent of max Health whenever any enemy unit dies near him — that is the thing Grievous Wounds is for. And Subjugate steals Health, Armor and Magic Resist, doubled over 4 seconds — none of which touches Noxian Guillotine, because Guillotine is true damage.
audit.corrected: Chomp restated as an Attack Damage sap on a 3.5s cooldown, attack speed attributed to Frozen Domain, King's Tribute named as the sustain, and the true-damage point stated so a player does not fear a stolen-armour Guillotine.
sources: audits/top/trundle__darius.json (reached the same true-damage conclusion from the other side)

audit.whatIsWrong: breakdown.cooldowns is a PDF-extraction run-on ending in the page artefact '• • Darius Top Lane Matchup Database 78' and carries no numbers. dosFull[0] tells you to 'bait' a stat steal without saying how long it is down for.
audit.why: Chomp at 3.5s is not baitable and the entry implies it is; the punishable cooldowns are Pillar of Ice (21s at rank 1), Frozen Domain (18s) and Subjugate (120s). Apprehend's own 26s at rank 1 is the window you are protecting.
audit.corrected: Rewritten with the real cooldowns and the page artefact removed.

audit.whatIsWrong: Pillar of Ice is described as a 'reposition' and a thing that 'denies your E stick', never as terrain, and no range is given.
audit.why: Riot's text: it 'creat[es] an ice pillar at target location, becoming impassable terrain and slowing all nearby enemy units', thrown from 1000 range. A player who thinks it is a slow will try to walk through it; a player who knows it is real terrain walks around before it finishes rising.
audit.corrected: Named as impassable terrain at 1000 range in dontsFull[1] and breakdown.early.

notes: Level-chart divergence worth a human eye: the Darius packet gives Darius/Darius/Darius/Darius/Darius/Darius/Trundle, the Trundle packet gives Darius/Darius/Darius/Skill/Trundle/Trundle/Skill, and both champions' files currently hold the identical third array Darius/Darius/Skill/Darius/Skill/Darius/Darius. I followed my own packet because all seven of this entry's whys already describe exactly that chart; the Trundle-side auditor marked their point 2 'correct' and proposed no chart edits, so the mirror will need mirror-fix.js to settle levels 4-5 and 6. Win-rate mismatch: Darius packet 54.45% over 1078 games (the Trundle-side auditor reports packets/trundle.json at 51.91 over 418 and MC_WR_TABLES.trundle.darius at 45.48 — three different numbers for one matchup). Not editable from here, but the spread is large. The _missing rule 'Trundle can deny your mobility (Noxian Guillotine (R)) with Pillar of Ice (E)' was NOT written in: Pillar of Ice is genuinely impassable terrain, but whether it blocks a target-locked leap like Guillotine is not answerable from the kit files and I would not assert it. breakdown.wave and breakdown.trading carry the shared PDF-extraction run-on; left untouched for consistency with the garen/gnar/riven/rumble/teemo entries.
